item.title: Parkinson urges Leadership Fiji graduates and alumni to make a difference in their communities
item.description: As 26 members of the Leadership Fiji 2026 programme celebrate their graduation, Leadership Fiji founder and Chair William Parkinson is urging them to take responsibility for shaping the country's future and making a difference in their communities. Speaking at the graduation and the organisation's 25th anniversary celebration, Parkinson says leadership is not about holding a position, but about ta
item.content:encoded:
As 26 members of the Leadership Fiji 2026 programme celebrate their graduation, Leadership Fiji founder and Chair William Parkinson is urging them to take responsibility for shaping the country's future and making a difference in their communities.

Speaking at the graduation and the organisation's 25th anniversary celebration, Parkinson says leadership is not about holding a position, but about taking action and making a difference every day.

He says the 26 graduates are now part of a growing network of 662 people who have completed Leadership Fiji's core programme over the past 25 years.

Parkinson says the organisation is now looking towards generational change, with its graduates expected to play a greater role in taking Fiji forward.

He believes leadership is not only about having the courage to stand up and lead, but also knowing when to step aside and allow the next generation to take responsibility.

Reflecting on the organisation's beginnings, Parkinson says Leadership Fiji was established following the political unrest of 2000, when many people were concerned about the country's future.

He says the events of that year highlighted the need to develop leaders who understood the importance of building a modern, multiracial and multireligious Fiji.

Parkinson says a meeting with representatives of Leadership Victoria in Melbourne helped inspire the establishment of Leadership Fiji, with a vision to prepare people who could lead the country towards a better future.

He says 25 years later, the organisation continues to invest in developing leaders who can bring positive change to their workplaces, communities and the country.

Parkinson also reminds the graduates that leadership must be guided by values rather than political divisions, particularly at a time when misinformation and political uncertainty are affecting societies around the world.

He encourages the graduates to carry Leadership Fiji's values of leadership, excellence, adaptability, diversity, empowerment, respect and service as they take on new responsibilities and continue their fellowship projects.

Meanwhile, Leadership Fiji has also launched its Youth Leadership and Career Pathway Programme this year, attracting around 225 participants from across the country.

The organisation plans to expand the programme next year and is also working towards establishing a permanent leadership centre, with the aim of creating a regional hub for leadership training in the Pacific.

item.title: Over 8,000 suspected marijuana plants uprooted in the North and meth seized in Laucala Beach
item.description: More than 8,000 plants believed to be marijuana have been uprooted from two farms in the Lea farming area in the Cakaudrove Province following an operation by the joint Northern Division Taskforce. Police say the operation was conducted this week, with officers from the RFMF supporting the taskforce as they trekked through the farming terrain and discovered the two farms.
item.content:encoded:
More than 8,000 plants believed to be marijuana have been uprooted from two farms in the Lea farming area in the Cakaudrove Province following an operation by the joint Northern Division Taskforce.

Police say the operation was conducted this week, with officers from the RFMF supporting the taskforce as they trekked through the farming terrain and discovered the two farms.

Meanwhile, Police drug operations have also resulted in the seizure of suspected methamphetamine and cash believed to be proceeds of crime in Laucala Beach.

Police say officers from the Police Dog Unit raided the home of a 39-year-old man, where several zip-lock bags containing white substances believed to be methamphetamine were seized.

Police also seized cash during the raid, which they suspect came from criminal activities.

Police say drug operations are continuing across the five policing divisions, with arrests being made for unlawful possession of illicit drugs and related offences, including proceeds of crime.

item.title: Suspect in custody over destruction of Lord Ganesh statue in Ba
item.description: A suspect is in custody following the destruction of a Lord Ganesh statue at the Shri Maha Devi Gangaman Temple in Field 28, Rarawai, Ba. Police have confirmed the suspect is the same person arrested in Nadi earlier this year for allegedly committing a similar offence.
item.content:encoded:
A suspect is in custody following the destruction of a Lord Ganesh statue at the Shri Maha Devi Gangaman Temple in Field 28, Rarawai, Ba.

Police have confirmed the suspect is the same person arrested in Nadi earlier this year for allegedly committing a similar offence.

Police say a report was lodged in Ba and an investigation was conducted, leading to the suspect being taken into custody.

The alleged incident happened just days before Diwali, leaving the temple committee and the wider community devastated.

Temple Manager Munen Lingam says the temple committee discovered yesterday morning that the main Lord Ganesh statue was missing from its place, with the caretaker later finding pieces of the one-metre-high statue near a sacred fig tree.

Lingam says the statue had been broken against a stone, with some pieces placed in a sack and others thrown into a nearby creek.

He says this is the second time the temple has been targeted, following an incident in November when a Lord Hanuman statue was damaged and stolen.

Lingam says security at the temple had been strengthened following the previous incident, with additional grills and shutters installed, and plans to install CCTV cameras.

However, he says those responsible managed to cut the lock and damage the grill protecting the Lord Ganesh statue before destroying it.

Lingam says nothing else was stolen or damaged during the latest incident, and the small amount of money left by devotees at the temple was untouched.

He says the incident has deeply affected the temple committee, Ramayan Mandali and families from Field 28 and surrounding communities, particularly as devotees regularly gather there for prayers and religious activities.

Lingam says the community had been preparing for its Diwali celebrations, including a programme scheduled for Saturday, and many are now struggling to understand why the incident happened.

He says the community does not want the incident to create divisions between religions or races.

item.title: Diwali excitement builds as families complete festive preparations
item.description: The excitement of Diwali is taking over as families stock up on festive treats and make last-minute purchases ahead of the Festival of Lights. Taras Supermarket Director Amish Patel says preparations for Diwali have been going well, with excitement building as families get ready for the celebrations.
item.content:encoded:
The excitement of Diwali is taking over as families stock up on festive treats and make last-minute purchases ahead of the Festival of Lights.

Taras Supermarket Director Amish Patel says preparations for Diwali have been going well, with excitement building as families get ready for the celebrations.

Patel extends his Diwali wishes to everyone, hoping they enjoy a safe and joyous celebration.

Meanwhile, Manjula Sharma of Nadera says she came out to complete her final round of shopping before Diwali, having already finished cleaning her home and preparing sweets.

Sharma says she will be celebrating Diwali with her spouse and relatives.

She also reflects on how much she misses her children, who are living overseas, as she celebrates Diwali without them.

She also purchased silver utensils today to mark Dhanteras, saying buying silver on the occasion is considered auspicious and is believed to bring good fortune.

Sharma wishes everyone a happy Diwali and reminds families to stay safe, particularly by keeping a close eye on children when they are using fireworks.

item.title: Government has not been sitting idly amid prolonged dry weather – Rabuka
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Government has not been sitting idly in responding to the challenges caused by prolonged dry weather conditions. In a statement, Rabuka says that for months, the Government has been warning about the impact of El Niño.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka says the Government has not been sitting idly in responding to the challenges caused by prolonged dry weather conditions.

In a statement, Rabuka says that for months, the Government has been warning about the impact of El Niño.

He says the Government has also been raising Fiji's concerns at international climate conferences, including COP, and calling on the world's major economies to recognise the challenges faced by small island nations like Fiji.

Rabuka says the Government has repeatedly warned that climate change is not a distant threat.

He further says its consequences are already being felt by people across Fiji, with communities experiencing water shortages.

The Prime Minister says he understands the difficulties this is causing families, farmers and businesses.

He adds that the Water Authority of Fiji has been working every day to maintain water supplies and deliver water to affected communities.

Rabuka says that according to the latest figures presented to Parliament, 67 water trucks have been deployed.

He says more than 885,000 litres of water have been delivered by road since 30th October, while another 810,000 litres were delivered by sea between 30th September and 30th October.

He says disaster management teams, regional development officials and other Government agencies have also been responding, coordinating assistance and preparing for conditions that may become more difficult in the months ahead.

The Prime Minister says the Government has been preparing for this situation for months and will continue to strengthen its response as necessary.

Rabuka adds that the scale of the drought is serious, and while the Government cannot control the weather or make it rain, it can prepare, mobilise resources and do everything possible to protect the people.

He says this is also why the Government continues to advocate internationally for greater climate financing and assistance.

The Prime Minister says small countries like Fiji cannot be expected to carry the growing burden of climate change alone.

Rabuka says the international community needs to recognise what people in Fiji are experiencing and support the country's efforts to build resilience.

He further says some may choose to take his words out of context and use them to score political points, and they are free to do so.

However, he says that while others debate his words, Government teams are out there delivering water and helping communities.

Rabuka says this is a difficult period for the country, and it calls for solidarity, cooperation and a shared determination to look after one another.

He says Fiji will get through this together.
